text: Mowalola Ogunlesi (born 25 March 1994) is a Nigerian-born fashion designer and singer based in London. She is known for using a wide variety of textiles such as leather and PVC to create non-traditional silhouettes inspired by Nigerian and London youth culture. Ogunlesi was born to a Nigerian-Scottish mother and a Nigerian father; she is of Yoruba ethnicity. Both of her parents are fashion designers—her mother, Adenike Ogunlesi of Ruff 'n' Tumble, specializes in children's clothing, and her father works in traditional Nigerian menswear. At the age of 12, she moved from Nigeria to attend boarding school in the Surrey countryside. She earned her Bachelor of Arts in Fashion from Central Saint Martins – University of the Arts London, debuting a collection at the Graduation Press Show in 2017. She enrolled in the Master of Arts programme at Central Saint Martins that year but dropped out in 2018 to gain more creative freedom. After leaving Central Saint Martins, she applied to the Fashion East mentorship and support programme, and her 2019 London Fashion Week debut took place on Fashion East's stage. In September 2019, she came under scrutiny when Naomi Campbell was spotted wearing a Mowalola gown with a bullet wound design; the dress was interpreted as a statement on gun violence, but on Instagram Ogunlesi clarified it was meant to convey a sense of being a walking target. In October 2020, Ogunlesi was named by Elle as one of "10 Trailblazing Women Changing The Future You Need To Know," alongside Tobi Kyeremateng, Ngozi Onwurah, Simi Lindgren, Balanda Atis, Magdalene Abraha, Koffee, Holly Fischer, Celeste, and Margaret Busby. In 2019, she created outfits for Skepta's "Pure Water" music video and was one of six designers approached by British Vogue to style Barbie dolls for the brand's 60th anniversary. On 26 June 2020, the Yeezy Gap 10-year partnership was officially announced, with Ogunlesi appointed by Ye as design director. In 2022, she joined MGA Entertainment as a designer for a line of their Bratz dolls featuring Jade and Felicia, which was released on 1 December. In 2025, she collaborated with The Skateroom to design a limited-edition skateboard deck collection. Ogunlesi also releases music under the name Mowalola; in 2021, she released two singles, "Truck" and "Wawa," and was featured on Namasenda's single "Banana Clip" (2021). In 2024, she directed the visual for JT's single "Okay" and starred in FKA Twigs' music video for "Perfect Stranger."
